snippet.title: Every Type Of Shotgun Shell Explained
snippet.description:
Every Type Of Shotgun Shell Explained

From birdshot and buckshot to slugs, flechettes, and dragon's breath, this video breaks down every type of shotgun shell ever made — covering their design, history, ballistics, and real-world performance. Whether you're into hunting loads like #5 and #6 birdshot for pheasant and waterfowl, defensive rounds like double-aught buckshot, or military experiments like flechette shells from the Vietnam War era, we cover the full spectrum of 12 gauge, 20 gauge, and 10 gauge ammunition types. We also dive into improvised rounds like cut shells and wax slugs, specialized loads like API armor-piercing incendiary shells, flight control wads like Federal Premium's FliteControl, and less-lethal options used by law enforcement — including beanbag rounds, rubber slugs, and foam batons. If you play games like Hunt: Showdown, Escape from Tarkov, Ready or Not, or Battlefield and want to actually understand what you're loading into that shotgun, this one's required viewing. From Foster slugs and sabot slugs to mini shells, buck and ball, and flare rounds — this is the most complete shotgun ammunition guide on YouTube.

snippet.title: How Cappadocian People Built Hidden Underground Cities (For 20,000 People)
snippet.description:
Deep beneath the surface of Cappadocia lies one of the most astonishing engineering feats in history vast underground cities carved entirely from rock, capable of housing tens of thousands of people.

In this video, we explore how ancient communities created these massive hidden cities, complete with ventilation systems, water supplies, storage rooms, and defensive structures all without modern tools.

You’ll Discover:
How soft volcanic rock made large-scale excavation possible
The ingenious ventilation shafts that supplied fresh air deep underground
Hidden doors and tunnels designed for defense
How entire communities lived, cooked, and stored food below ground
Why these cities were built in the first place

Places like Derinkuyu Underground City reveal a level of planning and survival strategy that still amazes engineers today.

No machines. No electricity. Just precision, planning, and an incredible understanding of the environment.

Sometimes the most advanced cities… were the ones you couldn’t see.

5 Worst Scientific Failures Ever.


Discover the shocking stories behind three of history's most notorious scientific blunders! 🌌🚀 In this video, we delve into the Mars Climate Orbiter tragedy, lost due to a simple unit conversion error between metric and imperial measurements. Next, we explore the Hubble Space Telescope's initial failure, where a flaw in its mirror necessitated a critical repair mission to fix blurry images. Lastly, we uncover the dark history of Thalidomide, a so-called "wonder drug" that tragically led to severe birth defects before being pulled from the market. Learn how these errors happened and their profound impacts.

snippet.title: Why We Stopped Eating 15 Medieval Vegetables... It Wasn't the Taste, It Was Control
snippet.description:
Medieval diets included dozens of vegetables that have almost disappeared from modern plates. But they didn’t vanish because they tasted bad.

In this video, we uncover 15 forgotten medieval vegetables and the surprising reasons they disappeared from agricultural control and industrial farming to changing markets, storage demands, and the rise of mass-produced food.

🌿 You’ll Discover:

The hardy crops peasants relied on for survival

Why some nutritious vegetables were pushed out of the food system

How large-scale farming changed what we eat today

Which forgotten foods might actually be better for health and sustainability

This isn’t just food history it’s the story of how modern agriculture reshaped our diet.

snippet.description:
Every WW2 Country's Infantry Loadout RANKED | Part 3

From the Krag-Jørgensen bolt-actions of Norway to the fully modernized M1 Garand-equipped Brazilian Expeditionary Force, Part 3 of our WW2 infantry loadout series digs into eight more nations whose small arms told very different stories about readiness, improvisation, and firepower. We're covering the Mannlicher-Schönauer M1903 of Greece, Yugoslavia's patchwork partisan arsenal of MP40s, Sten guns, and PPSh-41s, Czechoslovakia's world-class vz.24 and ZB vz.26 that Germany seized and turned against the Allies, India's Vickers-Berthier and SMLE combo forged at Ishapore, South Africa's Thompson-heavy desert loadout, New Zealand's ultra-rare Charlton Automatic Rifle conversion, and Brazil's full American kit in the Italian Gothic Line campaign. Whether you're here for the historical deep-dive, the obscure prototype rabbit holes like the Czech ZH-29 or the Greek EPK, or you play Hell Let Loose, Post Scriptum, Hearts of Iron IV, or IL-2 Sturmovik and want the real-world context behind the weapons, this one's got you covered. If you missed Parts 1 and 2, check those out first — each nation's loadout tells a story that goes way beyond just the rifle in their hands. snippet.title: Every Army That Tried to Destroy Rome

And yet Rome kept coming back. In this video, we break down every major army that tried to destroy Rome, from the Gauls who sacked the city in 390 BC, to Hannibal's devastating victory at Cannae, to Attila the Hun's march on Italy, and finally the collapse that ended it all. What made each threat different. Why most of them failed. And what Rome's resilience actually tells us about power, adaptation, and the limits of empire.

snippet.title: What Marriage in Ancient Thailand Was Really Like (It's Worse Than You Think)
snippet.description:
They poured water, burned incense, and blessed the couple in the Buddha’s name. But behind the silk and ceremony, marriage in ancient Siam was anything but sacred. It wasn’t about love — it was about power, obedience, and control.

Behind every offering was a transaction. Behind every bow, a bargain. Daughters were bartered like treasure, their value weighed in silver, silk, and elephants. Inside the gilded palaces of Ayutthaya, concubines served kings as living offerings — bound by laws so strict that even their posture in bed was dictated by palace code.

This wasn’t romance beneath golden spires. This was submission behind closed doors. A single mistake could bring exile, mutilation, or death — from the slicing of a nose to the horror of the horse punishment. Yet beyond the palace walls lay a cruel paradox: Siamese women could trade, own property, and run thriving businesses — freedoms few women in the world had — but marriage stripped them of the power they had earned.

From bridewealth and polygamy to ritualized obedience and the terrifying punishments for adultery, this is the story of marriage in the Ayutthaya Kingdom — a system built on beauty, fear, and control.

This is not the romance of ancient Siam.
This is obedience gilded in gold.
This is marriage as domination.

Welcome to History Blends.

snippet.title: The City That Literally Ate Itself: History’s Most Horrifying Siege
snippet.description:
They didn’t fall to the sword. They didn’t burn, drown, or vanish into the night.
No — the people of Suiyang died in a way so horrifying that even centuries later, it remains one of the darkest chapters in human history.

It began with honor. With loyalty. With the determination to hold the line for a dying empire.
But when the walls closed in and the food was gone, survival demanded the unthinkable.

This wasn’t just a siege — it was a descent into madness.
A city of tens of thousands trapped by an army twenty times their size.
A commander so loyal to his emperor that he chose starvation over surrender.
And when hunger stripped away every last shred of humanity… the city turned on itself.

Women. Children. Soldiers. Friends.
Each became part of an organized system of death — and survival.
By the end, there was nothing left to defend but the memory of honor, twisted into a nightmare of flesh and famine.

Yet even in this abyss, one question endures:
Was Zhang Xun a hero who sacrificed everything for the Tang dynasty — or a man who crossed a line beyond redemption?

This isn’t just a story of war.
It’s the story of how desperation devours morality.
And how a city, once proud and alive, literally ate itself to survive.

This is the Siege of Suiyang.
And this is what happens when civilization breaks.

Welcome to History Blends.

snippet.title: Trapped and Slaughtered: The Roman Disaster in Teutoburg Forest
snippet.description:
They built roads that still exist and laws that still shape our world. But when it came to war, the Romans fought like no one else. Their army didn’t just march — it calculated. It didn’t just kill — it crushed.

For centuries, Rome’s legions were an unstoppable force — disciplined, organized, and precise. But deep within the dark forests of Germania, that iron machine met something it couldn’t outthink: nature, betrayal, and rage.

This wasn’t a battle fought on open fields or in grand arenas. It was fought in choking rain, in endless mud, and beneath trees so thick they swallowed sunlight. Three legions marched in — more than twenty thousand men — led by a trusted ally who would turn out to be their executioner.

Arminius — raised by Rome, trained by Rome, and honored by Rome — used everything he learned to destroy it. His trap at Teutoburg Forest didn’t just wipe out an army; it shattered an empire’s illusion of invincibility.

This was no simple ambush. It was a masterpiece of deception — a three-day slaughter where discipline dissolved into chaos, formations collapsed into panic, and one of history’s mightiest forces was erased from the map.

Augustus himself would wander his palace in grief, crying out: “Varus, give me back my legions!” But the forests never gave them back.

This is the story of the day Rome’s power broke.
This is the betrayal that changed history.
This is Teutoburg Forest.

snippet.description:

snippet.title: Every Major Crusader State Explained
snippet.description: One Muslim general destroyed a Christian army of 20,000 knights in a single afternoon and walked straight into Jerusalem. Another group of Crusaders, sent specifically to fight Muslims, somehow ended up sacking a Christian city instead. The Crusader States were some of the most chaotic, unlikely, and fascinating political experiments in medieval history, and almost none of them survived long enough to matter. We're breaking down every major state, how they were built, how they fell, and the genuinely unhinged stories in between. From the county that lasted 52 years to the kingdom that held on for nearly two centuries against impossible odds.

snippet.title: WW2 US Tank Ranking | From Worst to BEST
snippet.description:
Every U.S. Tank of WW2 RANKED

We're ranking every major American tank of World War 2 — from the M22 Locust and M3 Stuart to the M4 Sherman, M26 Pershing, and M4A3E2 Sherman Jumbo — covering armor thickness, firepower, crew size, engine specs, and real combat performance across every theater. From the Stuart's first tank-vs-tank clash against Japanese Type 95 Ha-Go tanks in the Philippines to the Pershing's legendary duel with a Panther at Cologne Cathedral, and the Jumbo-led relief of Bastogne by Cobra King on December 26th 1944, this breakdown covers the M3 Lee, M5 Stuart, M24 Chaffee, and every Sherman variant including the M4A3E8 Easy Eight, the 76mm-armed wet stowage models, and the British Firefly with its 17-pounder gun. Whether you're rolling into battle in War Thunder, commanding armor in Hell Let Loose or Post Scriptum, or theorycrafting in Hearts of Iron IV, this is your complete guide to U.S. armored doctrine, Lend-Lease, and why 49,000 Shermans changed the course of the war. Every gun caliber, every millimeter of armor, every engine — the M4 Sherman, M26 Pershing, and the rest of America's tank arsenal, fully ranked and explained.

snippet.title: How a Coffee Shop Became the Most Powerful Insurance Empire on Earth
snippet.description:
They didn’t start in a skyscraper.
They didn’t begin with billions in capital reserves.

They began with coffee.

In a noisy London port city, merchants, sailors, and ship captains crowded into a small café. They came for the caffeine… but stayed for something far more valuable: information. And inside Edward Lloyd’s coffee shop, a handful of men would turn risk into an empire.

Here, voyages worth fortunes were gambled on storms, pirates, and wars. Here, names were signed under promises that could ruin or enrich a man overnight. And here, in the smoky air above steaming mugs, the world’s most powerful insurance market was born.

Over the centuries, it would survive fire, fraud, and near financial collapse. It would insure everything from oil tankers to satellites… even celebrity body parts. It would face scandals that bankrupted aristocrats, disasters that shook nations, and crises so deep it nearly vanished entirely.

Yet somehow, it endured — growing into a marketplace that doesn’t just insure ships anymore, but anything on Earth… and beyond.

How did a humble coffee house become the beating heart of global risk? How did Lloyd’s of London rise, fall, and rise again to become the most unusual and powerful insurance empire in history?

This is that story.

Welcome to History Blends.

In a noisy London port city, merchants, sailors, and ship captains crowded into a small café. They came for the caffeine… but stayed for something far more valuable: information. And inside Edward Lloyd’s coffee shop, a handful of men would turn risk into an empire.

Here, voyages worth fortunes were gambled on storms, pirates, and wars. Here, names were signed under promises that could ruin or enrich a man overnight. And here, in the smoky air above steaming mugs, the world’s most powerful insurance market was born.

Over the centuries, it would survive fire, fraud, and near financial collapse. It would insure everything from oil tankers to satellites… even celebrity body parts. It would face scandals that bankrupted aristocrats, disasters that shook nations, and crises so deep it nearly vanished entirely.

Yet somehow, it endured — growing into a marketplace that doesn’t just insure ships anymore, but anything on Earth… and beyond.

How did a humble coffee house become the beating heart of global risk? How did Lloyd’s of London rise, fall, and rise again to become the most unusual and powerful insurance empire in history?

This is that story.

From nimble light tanks to a near-hundred-ton behemoth, Part 3 of our American WW2 tank breakdown covers six of the most fascinating armored vehicles the U.S. ever fielded — including the M2 Light Tank, M2 Medium Tank, Marmon-Herrington CTLS, LVT(A) Amtanks, Sherman Flame Tanks, and the monstrous T28 Super Heavy Tank. We're diving deep into the development history, combat performance, and technical specs of each vehicle — from the twin-turreted "Mae West" M2A2 and the Guadalcanal-tested M2A4, to the CTLS tankettes that fought and failed in the Dutch East Indies, to the amphibious LVT(A)-1 and LVT(A)-4 Amtanks that stormed the beaches of Saipan, Iwo Jima, and Okinawa. We also cover the 713th Tank Battalion's devastating Sherman flame tanks — given the same procurement priority as the B-29 and the atomic bomb — and the casemate-hulled T28, armed with a 105 mm T5E1 gun and twelve inches of frontal armor, that arrived too late for the Siegfried Line. Whether you're a WW2 armor historian, a War Thunder or World of Tanks player hunting for crew and vehicle research, or just a fan of American military engineering, this video is packed with the details you won't find anywhere else. If you missed Parts 1 and 2, check them out before diving in — this series covers every American tank from prototype to frontline service.

This video provides a deep dive into lesser-known American tanks that played crucial roles in military history, highlighting their development, unique features, and impact. From the early M2 Light Tank, which saw action with the Marine Corps at Guadalcanal and influenced later designs, to the M2 Medium Tank, a significant but ultimately superseded attempt at a modern combat vehicle, the evolution of American armor is explored.

The narrative also covers specialized vehicles like the Marmon-Herrington CTLS, an amphibious light tank adapted for the Marines and various international buyers, and the LVTA series of Amtanks, which transformed from civilian rescue craft into vital fire support for Pacific island hopping campaigns. The video also details the development and combat effectiveness of Sherman Flame Tanks, critical for infantry support in the Pacific, and the monumental T28 Super Heavy Tank, a prototype designed to breach the formidable Seigfried Line. These tanks, though sometimes obscure, each contributed to the broader narrative of American military innovation and adaptation during wartime.

snippet.title: The Brutal Fate of Female Pirates After Capture
snippet.description:
She wasn’t granted mercy because she was a woman.
She wasn’t spared the rope, the whip, or the cell.
No — her punishment was often harsher because she dared to live as something the world believed she should never be.

Dragged in chains through colonial ports, jeered at by crowds who saw her as both criminal and monster, she faced courts that didn’t need evidence — only a reminder that she had stepped outside her place. At Execution Dock, the sentence was not a swift drop but a slow strangling. A spectacle. A warning.

For others, the end came differently: the lash tearing across their backs in public squares; the iron of prison hulks rusting beneath their feet as disease crept through the darkness; the quiet horror of being sold into slavery, their identities erased as though they had never sailed at all. For female pirates, punishment was never just justice — it was correction. A way to reassert the order they had defied.

Because to the empires they robbed, and the societies that judged them, these women were not only thieves.
They were rebels against gender itself.

In this video, we uncover the shocking and often forgotten truth behind the fates of history’s most notorious female pirates. From Anne Bonny and Mary Read fighting to the last man on Calico Jack’s deck, to Rachel Wall becoming the final woman hanged in Massachusetts, to the countless women whose names barely survived — their ends reveal a world determined to crush those who stepped beyond the roles assigned to them.

Were they criminals? Symbols? Or simply women who refused to live quietly?

This is the story of piracy’s most defiant women — and the brutal punishments designed to erase them from the sea and from memory.

snippet.title: Through Fire and Blood: The Tragedy of Armenia
snippet.description:
"Through Fire and Blood: The Tragedy of Armenia" takes viewers on a gripping journey through one of the most harrowing chapters of human history. This documentary delves deep into the painful events of the Armenian Genocide, exploring the immense suffering, loss, and resilience of the Armenian people during the early 20th century. With rare footage, historical insights, and personal accounts, the video paints a vivid picture of a nation torn apart by war, betrayal, and atrocity.

As we trace the history of Armenia, the video highlights both the external and internal struggles the country faced. From the devastating massacres to the struggle for cultural survival, we witness the strength of a people determined to endure, despite the overwhelming odds. Through powerful visuals and narrative, the documentary reveals the personal and collective trauma that shaped the nation’s identity, while also honoring the spirit of hope and perseverance that arose from the darkest times.
